LAREDO — Eduardo Homero Ramos was booked into the Webb County Jail on Thursday night on alleged felony charges including manufacture or delivery of a controlled substance and aggravated assault with a deadly weapon, according to Webb County Sheriff's Office booking records.

Ramos was arrested on October 29, 2026, at 10:00 p.m. by the Webb County Sheriff's Office. The booking record lists manufacture or delivery of a controlled substance in Penalty Group 1 under one gram, a state jail felony; aggravated assault with a deadly weapon, a second-degree felony; and two counts of criminal mischief valued at $100 to less than $750, Class B misdemeanors. Bond had not been set on any of the charges.

A charge is an allegation, and every person is presumed innocent until proven guilty.

Update — November 6, 2026

Court records show the October 29 arrest followed a capias issued April 12, 2022, for failure to appear in case 2021CRD001031D3 in the 341st District Court, filed August 11, 2021, charging aggravated assault with a deadly weapon, a second-degree felony, and two counts of criminal mischief, Class B misdemeanors. The warrant was served October 30, according to the Webb County public-access court portal. The docket lists bond at $15,000 on the assault count and $500 on the mischief counts. A pre-trial hearing was held November 5, proposed conditions of probation were filed November 6, and a compliance hearing is set for January 19, 2027; the final pre-trial and jury selection dates were canceled, with an agreed resolution noted on the docket. The docket also lists a second active case, 2020CRL000674D3, filed May 6, 2020, for manufacture or delivery of a controlled substance in Penalty Group 1 under one gram. The charges remain allegations, and Ramos is presumed innocent until proven guilty.

Sources: Webb County Sheriff's Office Booking Jail Search; Webb County public-access court records.
